{{Term/Store|Shibo||Series, BotW, TotK}} is a recurring character in {{TLoZ Series}}.<ref>{{Cite|Shibo|Game Screen|BotW}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|Shibo|Game Screen|TotK}}</ref>

==Biography==
==={{BotW|-}}===
Shibo can be found at the [[Dueling Peaks Stable]] with his family. He normally stands outside with his twin brother, [[Darton]] outside the [[Horse]] pen beside the Stable. When approached, he speaks with Darton about whether [[Link]] is interested in Horses.<ref>{{Cite|{{Small|Hey, Shibo... You think this nosy guy right here is interested in horses?}}|Darton|BotW}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|{{Small|Looks like it to me, Darton... Judging from his eyes, he's just itching to get into the saddle.}}|Shibo|BotW}}</ref> The two conclude that he must then be a customer to the Stable.<ref>{{Cite|{{Small|That means...}}|Shibo|BotW}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|{{Small|THAT MEANS...}}|Darton|BotW}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|That means we've got ourselves a customer!|Darton|BotW}}</ref>

The two offer to share their knowledge of Horses with Link. Shibo offers insight on how to catch Horses by sneaking up on them.<ref>{{Cite|[Catching a horse...] Wild horses get scared easily, and if they notice people near them, they'll take off. Just sneak up on 'em from behind real slow. When you get good and close...grab 'em and jump on quick!|Shibo|BotW}}</ref> Shibo will also inform Link that spotted Horses possess an even temperament and are easy to tame whereas single-color horses are wilder and more difficult to train.<ref>{{Cite|[Good horses?] Horses with {{Color BotW|Blue|spots}} on them are even-tempered and easy to train. On the other hand, horses that are all {{Color BotW|Blue|one color}}, like straight black or white, are a bit more wild and harder to train.|Shibo|BotW}}</ref> Shibo and Darton's father, [[Rensa]], also gave the two advice on what kind of Horse is difficult to train, and which to start with.<ref>{{Cite|Dad said they're hard to handle at first, but if you spend a lot of time with a {{Color BotW|Blue|one-color}} horse, you'll be best buds!|Shibo|BotW}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|Dad also said that beginners should start with {{Color BotW|Blue|spotted}} horses... When I grow up, I'll ride a {{Color BotW|Blue|one-color}} horse, though!|Shibo|BotW}}</ref> When asked about how to train a Horse properly, Shibo points out that a Horse will not be obedient at first and must be soothed at first and when it performs well.<ref>{{Cite|They're really wild, so they'll run in different directions and buck here and there because they aren't trained yet. When that happens, you've gotta soothe them!|Shibo|BotW}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|The trick is to soothe them when they do what you want them to do. It's like saying "thanks" to them for a job well done!|Shibo|BotW}}</ref>

At night, Shibo will go inside the Stable to sleep. While asleep, Shibo will count spotted Horses.<ref>{{Cite|{{Small|One spotted horse... Two spotted horses...}}|Shibo|BotW}}</ref> When he wakes up, Shibo will attempt to beat Darton to the Horse pen.<ref>{{Cite|Today I'm gonna beat {{Color BotW|Blue|Darton}} to the place where the horses are!|Shibo|BotW}}</ref>

==={{TotK|-}}===
Shibo and his brother [[Darton]] can be seen outside of [[Dueling Peaks Stable]].
